lens: grid, alignment, margins and spacing, measured from layout.json

margins_mm.note: The top and bottom pass (±1 mm). The right margin passes only because the H2 rules reach 203.2 mm. The longest line of text ends at about 187 mm, so the ink margin on the right is 20.24 mm, 7.5 mm over the declared 12.7. The left side is the art rail and is exempt. The render reports margins_equal_within_1mm=false.

item_gap_mm.note: Everything is within ±0.5 mm. However, a 3-4 line cocktail block is separated from the next by 2.91 mm, about the same as the 2.65 mm gap between single-line rows, so the blocks have no stronger boundary.

price_right_edges_mm.note: Prices sit inline and have no shared column. In cocktails and spirits the price follows the name. In beer and wine it follows the tab-stop descriptor. That gives two inline behaviours on one page.

price_pair_scan.note: The name-to-price distance goes over 40% on 5 of the 7 tab-stop rows. It passes the gate only because the descriptor fills the gap on a single line.

column_fill.beer_wine_ink_ends_mm: 165-175 (about 30% of the column empty on the right)
column_fill.spirits_ink_ends_mm: about 135 (about 66% of the column empty on the right)

remove: The single-item subheads 'BRANDY · BRANDY' and 'SIDRA · CIDER'. 'Brandy · Brandy' repeats the same word, and 'Sidra' is already named in the H2 'Cerveza y Sidra'. Also shorten the H2 rules, which run about 16 mm past the longest line of text.
top_problem: Every left edge and the vertical rhythm measure well, but the right half of the reading column is empty canvas and the price has no fixed place: after the name in cocktails and spirits, after a descriptor in beer and wine, with price right edges 34.6 mm apart in one section. The page has no right edge. The missing big idea: Rob's rule has the art rail doing all the narrative work (it closely follows ref-01's vertical-wordmark-plus-sun-disk structure), and nothing from the loess and agave art system reaches into the menu column itself. There are no contour-strip section markers and no agave-leaf rules, so the column reads as a plain list set beside an illustration.
fixes: Give prices one fixed place. Either set beer and wine prices on a shared right tab near 175 mm (a 3-4 mm spread at most) and move cocktail and spirits prices to the same tab, or put every price directly after the name, with beer and wine descriptors on their own line.

Match the rule length to the text. Either end the H2 rules at about 187 mm, the longest ingredient line, or set the ingredient measure to fill the full 103.7 mm, so the right ink margin reads as 12.7 mm like the other three sides instead of 20.2 mm.
Separate cocktail blocks more clearly than single-line rows: use 1.5 units (10.5 pt) between blocks, or bring the beer and wine pitch down to 1 unit, rather than the current 2.91 mm against 2.65 mm.

Fix the Fraunces italic 'l' in the H2s. In the render, 'Cócteles' and 'Destilados' read as 'Cóctefes' and 'Destifados'. Turn off the alternate or swash, or choose a plainer italic cut, so the Spanish reads correctly in dim light.

Fill the empty spirits area and bottom-right corner with a device the column is missing (a shared price tab or leaders), or bring one element from the art system into the column, such as a contour-strip section mark in place of the plain H2 rules. Don't add ornament.

lens: typography and hierarchy, including the display wordmark and the bilingual heads

measurements.price_style: inline 1 em after name (cocktails, spirits) or after tabbed descriptor at 382 pt (beer, wine); no leaders
measurements.eye_travel_beer_wine: name right edge to price about 30-47 mm of a 103.7 mm column (about 29-45%), bridged by the descriptor, no leader or rule
measurements.dead_space: right third of the column (x about 172-203 mm) is empty from y 127 to 262 mm beside beer, wine and spirits; spirits block is 3 short rows in a 294 pt measure
measurements.item_gaps_pt: 7 within items, 7 plus 14 pt H3 at sub breaks, 14 plus 28 pt H2 block at section breaks

remove: the four full-width hairline rules under the H2 heads: the 17 pt bilingual head plus the 14 pt section gap already marks the break, and with the tracked caps H3s directly below, each section opens with three stacked devices
top_problem: The type system has no clear middle level. The 96 pt hairline CANTINA jumps straight down to 17 pt H2s, which are only 1.55x the 11 pt item names. The 9 pt DM Sans tracked caps serve line (LIME WHEEL · ROCKS) uses the same face, size, case and tracking as the H3 subheads, so garnish lines read as section labels. The Fraunces italic 'l' in the Spanish heads renders like a long-s ('Cócteſes', 'Destiſados'), and redundant bilingual pairs (BRANDY · BRANDY; DESTILADOS DE AGAVE · AGAVE under Destilados · Spirits) look unedited. The boldest missing idea: let the bilingual pairing be the typographic concept, for example the Spanish set large in a display italic that echoes the CANTINA cut and the English as a small roman gloss, instead of two equal halves joined by a bullet.
fixes: Make the serve line clearly different from the H3s: set it in Fraunces small caps or lowercase italic at 9 pt in the muted ingredient colour, with no DM Sans tracked caps, so only section labels use tracked sans caps.

Build a real H2 level: raise the Spanish half to about 22-24 pt in the Fraunces display optical size with the English as a smaller roman gloss, and turn off the swash/WONK italic 'l' (font-variation-settings 'WONK' 0, or ss01 off) so Cócteles and Destilados read correctly.

Cut duplicate bilingual labels: print 'Brandy' once (or 'Coñac'), drop 'DESTILADOS DE AGAVE · AGAVE' to 'AGAVE' or 'De Agave' so it no longer repeats the H2, and stop tracking the italic Spanish caps at 0.16em (italic caps tracked that wide look spindly; use roman caps or lowercase italic).

Fill the dead right third beside beer, wine and spirits: move beer/wine/spirit prices to one right-aligned tabular column at the rule end (576 pt) with a dotted leader in #9C8B7B, or narrow the lower sections' measure and add a second tab so the rows span the column.

Tie the wordmark to the menu: set '& Cocktail Bar · Iowa City, Iowa' in the same Fraunces as CANTINA (small caps, not DM Sans), and let the sun or an agave leaf tip cross behind the C or the final A so the art and the wordmark read as one lockup rather than three parallel strips.

lens: palette, contrast over the art, price and number styling

margins_text_ink_mm.note: The H2 rules reach 576 pt (12.7 mm right), so the frame measures correctly. Text ink stops 7.5 mm short of it, and in the lower half short by about 29 mm (beer, wine and spirits prices end at 164.6-174.2 mm against a 203.2 mm column edge).

measurements.price_systems: Two different systems: cocktails and spirits have the price inline 1 em after the name (x 122-161 mm). Beer and wine have the price hung after a tab-stopped descriptor (x 160.5-174.2 mm), so prices in the same section drift by up to 5.6 mm (Czech Pilsner 165.1 vs Dry Cider 171.6).
measurements.type_column_palette_use: Near-black plus one rust. Gold and all four agave greens appear only in the art, never in the type.

remove: The four full-width H2 hairlines. They run to 203 mm while the beer, wine and spirits content stops near 174 mm, which frames and advertises the empty right-hand void. Also drop the redundant 'BRANDY · BRANDY' subhead.
top_problem: Prices are the weakest-styled element on the page, and they are not one system. They are set in the same muted #5A4B3F as the italic sensory line, at the same size as the names, lighter than both names and ingredients, so the numbers recede instead of standing out. They also switch between inline-after-name (cocktails, spirits) and floating-after-descriptor (beer, wine), which leaves ragged, remote-feeling figures and a dead right-hand strip. The boldest missing idea is a type column that speaks the art's palette. The agave green and sun gold never cross the torn edge, so the art reads as a pasted-on poster rather than the menu's own ink. Beside ref-01 (a close structural cousin: vertical wordmark, sun disc, left art rail) this is cleaner but thinner in materiality, and it lacks ref-01's disciplined tabular price column.
fixes: Use one price system: set every price in a single tabular-lining column at a fixed tab close to the text (for example 470 pt, with the H2 rules shortened to match). Otherwise put beer and wine prices inline after the name like the cocktails, with the descriptor moved to the next line.

Give prices their own ink and weight, not the sensory-italic brown. For example, deep agave green #27463A (about 8.5:1 on the cream) at weight 600, or the rust #9A3B22 at 600. That separates numbers from description and carries the art's palette into the type.
Carry one more art colour across the torn edge, for example agave green for the H2 middle dot or the prices, so the palette reads as one 3-4 colour system rather than 'art colours' vs 'type colours'.

Close the right-hand dead field in beer, wine and spirits. Either shorten the column measure and rules to where the content ends, or widen the tab stop so rows fill the measure; the current 29 mm void next to 14 short rows is empty canvas, not whitespace.

Make the 'landed in Iowa' claim visible or drop it: the loess bluffs read as generic Southwest mesas, and the striped contour band at the foot reads muddy at print size. Simplify it to 3 strips with a clearer value step, so the art has one quiet zone.

lens: design concept and art direction (15, 16) against ref-02, ref-solstice and national bar-menu bar

measurements.price_style: inline, 11 pt after the last word; beer/wine prices trail a tab-stop descriptor at 382 pt, so prices float between 455 and 494 pt: no column and not beside the name
measurements.name_to_price_frac_note: Dry Cider 0.519, Malbec 0.458 and Amber Lager 0.454 are over 40% with no leader or rule. The descriptor bridges the gap, so association passes, but only just
measurements.margin_note: Left is the art rail, which is fine. Right ink sits 7.5 mm inside the declared margin: the beer, wine and spirits rows end around 494 pt of 576, leaving a dead band about 30 mm wide down the lower right
measurements.item_gaps_pt: 7 / 21 constant on the 7 pt unit; section gaps 13.99 x3 then 12.42 before the allergen line (1.57 pt off)
measurements.width_budget: art rail plus wordmark lane take about 46% of the page width; the reading column is 103.7 mm
measurements.glyph_issue: The Fraunces italic 'l' in 'Cócteles' and 'Destilados' renders with a crossbar, so the heads read as 'Cóctefes' / 'Destifados' (long-s / f lookalike) at the preview size

top_problem: This is ref-02 panel 2 again: sun disc plus agave on cream, with CANTINA turned vertical. The 'landed in Iowa' half of the thesis does not show. The contour strips read as generic striped desert hills, not Iowa loam, and the image fails the substitution test, since any Southwest cantina could use it. The boldest missing idea is making the meeting of Iowa and Mexico structural rather than scenic: for example, let the contour-plough rows run out of the collage and become the menu's own row rules and section bands, so the art and the list are one field.
remove: The four full-width H2 underline rules. They are the only devices that do not trace to the thesis, they cut the column into form-like bands, and the torn edge and bilingual heads already separate the sections.
fixes: Change the Fraunces italic 'l' in the Spanish H2s (turn off the WONK/alternate glyph or the stylistic set), so 'Cócteles' and 'Destilados' no longer read as 'Cóctefes' and 'Destifados'.

Make the Iowa half visible and structural: extend the contour-plough strips (or another unmistakably Iowa form, such as corn rows or loess bluffs with a river line) out of the rail into the menu field as section bands or row rules, so the image fails a swap test for any generic desert art.

Give the collage real paper materiality at actual size: vary tear direction and fibre width per layer, add one consistent paper grain across all cut shapes (not only the sky and sun), and add one tonal overlap or shadow per layer. At the moment the uniform white-fibre edge on every strip reads as a vector filter, far below Solstice's layered depth.

Fix the dead lower-right band and the floating beer/wine prices: either set the descriptor and price on fixed tab stops (price right-aligned at one x within 40% of the name) or put the descriptor on its own line under the name with the price inline. Either way the short rows use the measure and the prices share one edge.

Tighten the width budget: narrow the wordmark lane or pull the reading column left by 8-10 mm, so the right text margin matches the 12.7 mm top and bottom and the column stops reading as pushed into the right half.

measurements.price_style: two inline styles: cocktails and spirits have the price after the name; beer and wine have it after a tabbed description at x=382pt, so prices are ragged at 357-494pt
measurements.eye_travel: inline, short everywhere, so no remote-price flag
measurements.line_box_margins_pt: top 31.88 / right 576 / bottom 756.16: the line boxes sit on the 36pt margin, and the ink-right shortfall comes from the ragged right edge, not from a margin error
measurements.phone: single column; hero crops the agave, sun and mesas and loses the torn page edge that carries the 'sun behind the page' thesis in print; H2 goes from print's inline 'Cócteles · Cocktails' to two stacked lines; the torn-strata footer repeats as a bookend; beer and wine keep the fixed tab column, so the phone price x is ragged

remove: The redundant bilingual H3 pairs where both halves say the same thing ('BRANDY · BRANDY', 'DESTILADOS DE AGAVE · AGAVE' under the 'Destilados' H2). Drop the echo, or drop the H3 where a section has one group.
top_problem: Print and phone share a palette and type system but not a concept. The phone loses the torn-page rail, the one idea that makes the print ownable, and gets a generic centred desert-sun hero, so the phone reads like a Southwest poster over a clean list. On both formats the prices use two different placements (after the name, and after the tabbed description), a table-like row with a ragged price edge. Boldest missing idea: make the torn Iowa contour-strip field the menu's actual structure (each section a furrow band that the agave grows out of, on paper and as the phone's scroll rhythm) instead of trim at the edges.
fixes: Unify price placement: either put every price inline after the name (move beer and wine prices before the style note) or give beer and wine a true tabular price column with tabular figures at one x, on print and phone alike.

Carry the torn vertical page edge into the phone: tear the hero bottom as a ripped sheet over the cream ground, not a horizontal strata band, so the phone keeps the print's 'sun behind the page' gesture.

Use the torn contour strips as section dividers on the phone (a thin torn band between Cocktails, Beer, Wine and Spirits) in place of the hairline H2 rules, so the art system organises the content instead of just framing it.
Give H3s more space above than below (14pt above, 3-4pt below), so 'DE LA CASA' and 'SIDRA' stop hugging the previous item's garnish line; the 7pt gap reads the same as an item break.

Make the phone H2 the same bilingual treatment as print ('Cócteles · Cocktails' on one line at the phone's column width), and set prices a step bolder or in the rust accent, so numbers are styled rather than left as grey body text.

lens: every item and price vs build/draft_doc.json (rev 3)
top_problem: All 14 prices and names match the draft exactly. Nothing is invented or dropped: Junmai Ginjo is retired, the Manhattan bitters are hidden by public_components, and garnish and glass come from recipe_versions. The content still reads as three different menus. Cocktails use a stacked name+price over ingredients and a garnish/glass line. Beer and wine use a tabbed name, then a descriptor, then a trailing price, so the price right edges spread 136 pt across the page. Spirits are bare name+price. The beer and wine descriptors are near-tautologies ('dry red wine' for Malbec, 'hop-forward IPA' for Dry-Hopped IPA) with no region or ABV. The label 'BRANDY · BRANDY' reads as a bug, not a bilingual pair.
problems: Criterion 3: there are two price grammars. Cocktails and spirits put the price inline after the name. Beer, cider and wine put it after a descriptor at the 382 pt tab. Prices on the tabbed rows sit at ragged x positions (about 160-172 mm), so there is no shared price edge within a section, and the measured price_right_edge_spread is 136 pt.

Brut Rosé 13 prints with no glass/bottle label under 'Espumosos · Sparkling', while Malbec and Pinot Grigio get 'Por Copa · By the Glass'. A guest cannot tell whether 13 is a glass or a bottle (flagged as needs_input 5, but it is still unresolved in print).

Criterion 8: Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé have no region, and the beers and cider have no ABV. These are correctly flagged as missing_ingredients and not invented, but the printed descriptors ('dry red wine', 'dry white wine', 'hop-forward IPA') mostly restate the item name or category and add little for the guest.

Subheader 'BRANDY · BRANDY' repeats the same word in both languages, and 'Destilados · Spirits' over 'Destilados de agave · Agave' repeats 'Destilados'. Both weaken the bilingual system's credibility.

The Brown Butter Old Fashioned ingredient line wraps after 'house demerara syrup', so 'aromatic bitters' starts the next line with no middot separator. It reads as a separate line, not the third ingredient.

Criterion 5: the giant vertical CANTINA wordmark and the section H2s are a clear entry and path. But the cocktail block takes about 45% of the column, and beer, wine and spirits get progressively thinner treatment, so the categories are not treated equally in weight.

The title 'Cantina' stands in for an unknown venue name (the draft title is 'Bar menu', needs_input 8). The rail line '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA' states no item fact, so it passes, but the menu has no real venue identity yet.
fixes: Put every price in one position: either right after the name on the name line for all sections, including beer and wine (moving the descriptor to its own line below, as for cocktails), or at one shared right edge for the tabbed rows.
Label Brut Rosé's price 'copa' or 'botella' as soon as Rob answers needs_input 5, and until then print it under the 'Por Copa · By the Glass' convention only if that is confirmed; do not guess.
Rename 'BRANDY · BRANDY' to a single bilingual-correct label (for example 'Coñac · Cognac' or just 'Brandy'), and shorten 'Destilados de agave · Agave' to 'Agave' so the H2 is not repeated.
Keep the middot at line breaks in ingredient lists (end the first line with '·', or rebalance the measure) so 'aromatic bitters' reads as the third ingredient of the Brown Butter Old Fashioned.

Replace the tautological beer and wine descriptors with style + ABV (beer) and grape + region (wine) as soon as the needs_input 2-4 data arrive; until then, drop descriptors that only repeat the item name (for example 'hop-forward IPA' becomes 'hop-forward') rather than padding.

top_problem: The cocktails are complete and follow Rob's order. Every other category is thin. The four beers and the cider have no ABV or producer, and the three wines have no region. Their only descriptions are category labels ('dry red wine', 'dry white wine', 'hop-forward IPA'), which read like database classes. None of these gaps is shown on the page. They exist only in meta.missing. Price placement is also inconsistent: cocktails and spirits have the price right after the name, but in beer and wine rows the price trails a description of varying length, so those prices sit at ragged x positions. Brut Rosé 13 has no glass or bottle label.
problems: All 14 prices match the draft (15/15/16/14, 7/8/7/8, 12/11/13, 12/16/18). No item is invented or changed. Junmai Ginjo is rightly omitted (retired). The side rail ('CANTINA', '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA') is generic and states no item fact. There are no taglines.

Cocktail ingredients follow base → modifier → sweetener → citrus → bitters and trace to the recipe versions. The Manhattan prints only rye whiskey · sweet vermouth because its bitters are hidden by public_components. That is allowed, but it is the only cocktail with fewer than three printed components.
Margarita's sensory line 'Bright, citrus-forward' rewords the draft's 'Bright and citrus-forward.'. The fact is the same, but the wording is not verbatim.
Brown Butter Old Fashioned: the break before 'aromatic bitters' drops the '·' separator, so the second line reads as an orphan and not as the third ingredient.

Beer (Czech Pilsner, Dry-Hopped IPA, Amber Lager) and Dry Cider: the scorecard asks for style and ABV. ABV, brewery or producer, pour size and cider format are all missing, with no mark on the page. 'hop-forward IPA' repeats the name.

Wine: the scorecard asks for grape and region. The region is missing on all three wines. 'dry red wine' and 'dry white wine' are taxonomy words. Brut Rosé's price has no glass or bottle label (meta.missing: 'price label: glass or bottle'), and it sits outside the 'Por Copa' subhead, so the guest cannot tell which it is.
Spirits are name + price by Rob's rule. Still, the Blanco and Añejo age statements and the Cognac brand stay unknown and are not shown as missing anywhere a buyer would see.

Prices use three placements: inline after the name (cocktails, spirits), after a description tab column with a ragged x (beer and wine: the 7, 8, 7 and 8 and the 12, 11 and 13 each sit at different x), and no aligned column at all.

The subhead 'BRANDY · BRANDY' is a redundant bilingual pair. 'Destilados' followed by 'Destilados de agave' repeats itself. 'tequila blanco' in the Margarita and the item 'Blanco Tequila' use different word orders for the same spirit on one page.
fixes: Get ABV (and brewery or producer) for the three beers and the cider, and region for Malbec, Pinot Grigio and Brut Rosé, through needs_input. Until they arrive, make the missing_ingredients flag visible in the proof so the gaps are not buried in meta.
Label Brut Rosé's 13 as glass or bottle (from input, not assumed), or move it under a clearly labelled pour, so its price is unambiguous.

Put the beer and wine prices at one shared x, either right after the name as in the cocktails or at a fixed tab after a fixed-width description column, so the three price placements become one consistent system.
Fix the Old Fashioned line break so 'aromatic bitters' keeps its leading '·', or rebreak so the three ingredients read as one list.
Replace 'Brandy · Brandy' with one label (or 'Brandy · Coñac'), and make 'Blanco Tequila' and 'tequila blanco' use the same word order everywhere.

lens: flow and reading path for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City
top_problem: There are two price rules on one page, so the reader has no steady place to look for a price. Cocktails and spirits put the price after the name. Beer, cider and wine put it after the tab-stop descriptor, so it lands at a different x on every row (measured price right-edge spread is 136 pt across the column). The eye has to hunt for each price, and the top-heavy cocktail block (280 of about 725 pt) makes the lower sections read like an afterthought. Against the draft (build/draft_doc.json) all 14 items and prices match exactly. No item is invented. Junmai Ginjo is omitted correctly (retired). The rail text '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA' is generic and states no item fact. Gaps are flagged in meta.missing, not invented: beer ABV and brewery, wine region and producer, the Brut Rosé glass or bottle label, and spirit age or brand.
problems: Criterion 3: prices follow two inline rules. After the name for cocktails and spirits (x about 357-386 pt). After the descriptor for beer, cider and wine (x about 456-494 pt), where every row's price sits at a different x because descriptor lengths differ (e.g. 'hop-forward IPA 8' against 'dry sparkling cider 8'). You cannot scan a price column in any section below Cocktails.

Criterion 5: the reading path has three row patterns, one per stretch of the list. Cocktails use a stacked block of 3-4 lines. Beer, cider and wine use a three-part row (name, tab-stop descriptor, price). Spirits are a bare name and price. The grouping is clear but the rhythm changes at each section, and the cocktail block takes about 39% of the reading column, so Wine and Spirits look squeezed at the foot.

Criterion 5: in a Mexican cantina the agave list ('Destilados de agave') is the category guests expect to find, but it sits in the last slot with two bare rows and no more weight than 'Brandy'. That order is standard and acceptable. Still, the hierarchy does nothing to let the house's own category read as a group rather than a tail.

Criterion 5 and 10: the H3 'Brandy · Brandy' repeats itself, and 'Destilados de agave · Agave' repeats 'Destilados' from its own H2. The bilingual pattern is followed mechanically even where it adds a line of noise to the reading path.

Criterion 8: only the Margarita has a sensory line ('Bright, citrus-forward'), which is correct under Rob's rule because it is the only draft description. But in a 4-cocktail group, one italic line makes the Margarita look featured and the other three look unfinished.

Criterion 8: beer prints no ABV, wine prints no region, and the Brut Rosé price has no glass or bottle label. All are flagged in meta.missing / needs_input, not invented, so there is no gate failure. But the scorecard's 100-level content (beer style + ABV, wine grape + region) is not reached.

Criterion 8 and 10: 'Dry-Hopped IPA' followed by 'hop-forward IPA' repeats the name on the same row. The draft reads 'Hop-forward draft IPA'; the shortened descriptor keeps 'IPA' and drops the only new word ('draft'), so the descriptor adds nothing.

Criterion 10: the Old Fashioned ingredients break so that 'aromatic bitters' sits alone as a widow on line 2. The Old Fashioned is also the only cocktail whose ingredients take two lines. That breaks the otherwise even cocktail block.

Criterion 10: proposal.md still carries round-20 tables that contradict the render. Its Margarita line reads 'lime wheel · bright, citrus-forward ROCKS', the section gap is given as 21 pt, and layout.json item_gap_note also still says 21 pt. The documentation does not match what is printed.
fixes: Adopt one price rule for the whole menu: either put every price right after the item name (beer, cider and wine would become name + price, with the descriptor after the price or on the tab stop), or give beer, cider and wine one shared right-aligned price tab so their prices share one x per section.

In beer, cider and wine, cut the repeated word from descriptors that echo the name ('hop-forward IPA' → 'hop-forward, draft', from the draft's 'Hop-forward draft IPA'), and have the Coordinator get ABV for beer and region for wine so those rows can meet criterion 8.

Rebreak the Old Fashioned so no single ingredient is left alone (for example, set it in one line at the column measure, or break after 'brown butter-washed bourbon' so line 2 carries 'house demerara syrup · aromatic bitters').
Simplify the redundant bilingual H3s: when both languages share the word, print it once ('Brandy'), and use 'De agave · Agave' under 'Destilados'. This takes a line of noise out of the reading path.

Bring the Wine and Spirits sections up to the cocktail block's weight by using the space the collapsed section gaps freed (for example 7 pt more item gap in the three-part rows), and update proposal.md and layout.json so they describe the 14 pt gaps and the printed Margarita stack.

lens: voice and consistency of descriptions, bilingual headings, venue copy, venue-type fit
top_problem: The menu uses two description systems. Cocktails have a stacked block (the Margarita alone gets an italic sensory line). Beer and wine have a mid-row lowercase gloss that mostly just repeats the name: 'hop-forward IPA' under Dry-Hopped IPA, 'toasty amber lager' under Amber Lager, 'dry sparkling rosé' under Brut Rosé, 'dry red wine' under Malbec. On top of that, the bilingual heads are not really parallel. So the copy reads as a careful data dump, not one venue voice, and it does not yet sound like a Mexican cantina in Iowa City.
problems: Checked against build/draft_doc.json: all 14 items and prices match. There are no invented items, and Junmai Ginjo is correctly omitted as retired. The printed Margarita line 'Bright, citrus-forward' is a faithful re-wording of the draft's 'Bright and citrus-forward.' The rail copy ('& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA') and the allergen footer state no item facts, and there are no taglines or captions, so content_integrity passes.

Voice is inconsistent inside one section. The Margarita has a capitalised italic sensory line; the Manhattan, Old Fashioned and Daiquiri have none. The Margarita therefore looks finished and the other three look like they are missing copy. This follows Rob's rule, but it reads unevenly.

The beer and wine descriptions are taxonomy, not guest language, and they repeat the item name: IPA/IPA, Amber Lager/amber lager, Brut Rosé/dry sparkling rosé ('brut' already means dry), Malbec/dry red wine. They start lowercase, while the Margarita line starts with a capital: two case conventions.

Criterion 8 is incomplete on the page. No wine prints a region, no beer prints an ABV or brewery, and no spirit prints an age or brand. These gaps are flagged correctly in needs_input, not invented, but the printed menu does not yet meet 'beer = style + ABV, wine = grape + region'.

The bilingual H3 pairs are not equal status, despite what the proposal says. In print the Spanish is light italic and the English is bold roman, so the English visibly wins. 'Brandy · Brandy' is a dead duplicate. 'Destilados de agave · Agave' repeats the H2 'Destilados' and is lopsided. 'Sidra · Cider' repeats the H2 'Cerveza y Sidra'.

Item names clash with the Spanish frame. The heads are bilingual, but the draft names use English word order ('Blanco Tequila', 'Añejo Tequila'), while the Margarita ingredient line says 'tequila blanco'. The same spirit is written two ways on one page.

There are two inline price grammars. Cocktail and spirit prices follow the name; beer and wine prices follow the description. As a result, prices on one-line rows sit at four or more different x positions (7, 8, 7, 8, 12, 11, 13 all ragged), and in beer and wine the price attaches visually to the gloss, not the name. The format itself is consistent (integers, no $).
The Brut Rosé price (13) under 'Espumosos · Sparkling' has no glass or bottle label. It is flagged, but in print a guest cannot tell the pour.

Venue fit: the allergen footer is English only on an otherwise bilingual menu. The Old Fashioned's dairy (brown butter) has no item-level cue while it waits for confirmation. There is no non-alcoholic or agua fresca section, which a Mexican restaurant is expected to have, and nothing in needs_input asks for one. Agave, the venue's signature category, comes last with two generic tequilas.

The reading path is clear: the CANTINA wordmark, then Cócteles, then one top-down column. But four-line cocktail blocks against one-line beer and wine rows make the page's rhythm lurch at 'Cerveza y Sidra', and the cocktail blocks outweigh everything below them.
fixes: Put every beer and wine price in the same place as the cocktail prices (right after the name) and move the gloss to its own line or a consistent sub-position, so there is one price grammar and prices sit next to their names.

Replace name-repeating glosses with draft-sourced qualifiers only (drop 'IPA', 'amber lager', 'sparkling rosé' where the name already says it), use one case convention across all descriptions, and ask Rob for ABV, wine region and pour or glass labels through needs_input so criterion 8 can be met in print.

Make the bilingual H3s truly parallel (same weight, Spanish italic only) and fix the redundant pairs: 'Brandy · Brandy' becomes a single 'Brandy', 'Destilados de agave · Agave' becomes 'De Agave · Agave', and fold or rename 'Sidra · Cider' so it does not echo the H2.

Set the allergen footer bilingually ('Informe a su mesero sobre cualquier alergia · Please tell your server about any allergies.') to match the menu's voice, and add a needs_input asking whether the venue has non-alcoholic drinks or aguas frescas to list.

Add needs_input asking Rob for draft sensory lines for the Manhattan, Old Fashioned and Daiquiri, and for the preferred name order for the tequila items (Tequila Blanco vs Blanco Tequila), so the cocktail stack reads evenly and the spirit names match the Spanish frame.

lens: Ingredient, garnish, glassware and heading traceability (build/draft_doc.json, phg.recipe_versions via gateway log_id 262), description quality, venue fit, description and price layout

Use one price-to-name relationship across the whole menu: in Beer & Cider and Vino, put the price after the name as the cocktails do, and move the style descriptor to its own lower-case line below, which removes the 136 pt price-edge spread and the mid-column description tab (criterion 14; layout note for the designer).

Ask Rob for sourced sensory copy for the cocktails other than the Margarita and for beer style/ABV and wine grape/region, because 'dry red wine' and 'hop-forward IPA' are category words, not guest language, and the menu voice stays uneven until the draft has them (criteria 12 and 8; do not invent any).

Drop the duplicated 'BRANDY · BRANDY' H3 (write it once, or use 'Brandy · Coñac' only if the source supports it), keep Spanish H3 capitalisation consistent in the doc ('Por copa', 'De barril', 'De la casa' in sentence case), and put the still-missing Brut Rosé glass/bottle label at the top of Rob's queue (criteria 13 and 14).

lens: description quality and one guest-facing voice (TEST-1 round 20b, Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar, Iowa City IA)
top_problem: The menu has no single guest-facing voice. Only one of four cocktails gets a sensory line (Margarita, 'Bright, citrus-forward', from phg.menu_items.menu_description 'Tequila blanco, lime, orange liqueur, agave. Bright and citrus-forward.'). Every beer, cider and wine line is a database class that echoes the item name, and each one is set in the same roman as the cocktail ingredient lists: 'dry red wine' (Malbec), 'dry white wine' (Pinot Grigio), 'dry sparkling rosé' (Brut Rosé: brut already means dry), 'dry sparkling cider' (Dry Cider), 'hop-forward IPA' (Dry-Hopped IPA), 'toasty amber lager' (Amber Lager). 'Dry' is printed four times. This is the criterion-12 automatic-fail pattern: taxonomy wording that repeats the name. The facts are real, but the menu reads like an export of the draft, not like a bar talking to a guest.
problems: C12: 6 of the 7 beer/cider/wine descriptions are class labels or restate the name. Only 'crisp pale lager' (Czech Pilsner) adds anything, and it still reads as a style tag. Sources: phg.menu_items.menu_description for Malbec 'Dry red wine.', Pinot Grigio 'Dry white wine.', Brut Rosé 'Dry sparkling rosé.', Dry Cider 'Dry sparkling cider.', Dry-Hopped IPA 'Hop-forward draft IPA.', Amber Lager 'Toasty amber lager.', Czech Pilsner 'Crisp pale lager.' (gateway log_id 263). All trace, all weak.

C12/C10: two description grammars on one page. Cocktails put an italic muted sensory line above roman lowercase ingredients. Beer and wine put a roman lowercase descriptor inline between name and price, in the same treatment as the cocktail ingredient lists. A guest reads 'dry red wine' as the same kind of line as 'rye whiskey · sweet vermouth'. The italic sensory voice appears exactly once on the page.

C12: Manhattan, Brown Butter Old Fashioned and House Daiquiri have no sensory line (correct: the draft has none, per rv 9fb77eaa, 7095fd3d, 14d45e57 and menu_description). But the signature house drink, Brown Butter Old Fashioned, is the flattest item on the menu. This needs_input should be raised to Rob as a blocking copy gap, not treated as neutral.

C14: the Brown Butter Old Fashioned ingredient line wraps as 'brown butter-washed bourbon · house demerara syrup' / 'aromatic bitters'. The separator dot is lost at the break, so 'aromatic bitters' sits orphaned on its own line and reads like a third stack element next to the ORANGE PEEL · ROCKS serve line.

C14: the price-to-name relationship changes by section. Cocktails and spirits use name + price inline. Beer and wine use name, a tab column, the description, then the price, so the prices wander (price_right_edge_spread 136 pt in layout.json). Association still holds because the rows are short, but it is two systems on one page.

C13: the Spanish heads are compromised by the Fraunces italic 'l', which renders like a long s / f at display size. In the preview, 'Cócteles' and 'Destilados' read as 'Cóctefes' and 'Destifados'. That is a misread of the host language on the two most visible Spanish words.

C13: redundant bilingual pairs. 'BRANDY · BRANDY' says nothing twice. 'DESTILADOS DE AGAVE' sits directly under 'Destilados · Spirits' and repeats the head. A cantina would say 'Agave' / 'Tequila y Mezcal' and 'Brandy / Coñac'.

C13: for a Mexican restaurant, agave carries only one of four cocktails and two of three spirits, and there are no Mexican beers (Czech Pilsner, IPA, Amber Lager). The draft sets the list (not a designer defect), but the copy does nothing to anchor the venue, e.g. no Spanish or agave-forward description voice.

C11: every printed ingredient, garnish and glass traces. Margarita: Lime wheel / Rocks, rv f06abb74. Manhattan: Cocktail cherry / Coupe, rv 9fb77eaa; aromatic bitters hidden per public_components. Old Fashioned: Orange peel / Rocks, rv 7095fd3d. Daiquiri: Lime coin / Coupe, rv 14d45e57, with 'house demerara syrup' from the rv note 'House 1:1 demerara syrup by weight.' Two paraphrases are acceptable but not exact to source: 'fresh lime' for ingredient 'Fresh Lime Juice', and 'house demerara syrup' on the Old Fashioned (component 'Demerara Syrup', role 'House prep / sweetener'). No invented facts. Known gap: ABV, region and brand are absent pending Rob's input, which keeps 11 below 80.

The side rail '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA' is generic venue copy with no item fact. The legal line is generic. Until then, flag every one of them as needs_input rather than printing class labels that echo the name.
Give beer and wine descriptors the same italic muted sensory treatment as the Margarita line, so one description voice runs through the whole menu and descriptors never look like ingredient lists.

Fix the Brown Butter Old Fashioned wrap: carry the '·' separator to the start of the second line, or rebalance the break (e.g. 'brown butter-washed bourbon' / '· house demerara syrup · aromatic bitters'), so 'aromatic bitters' is not orphaned (designer note; layout is not mine to change).
Replace or de-swash the italic 'l' in the Spanish display heads (use a stylistic set or the roman) so 'Cócteles' and 'Destilados' cannot be misread as 'Cóctefes' and 'Destifados'.

lens: Venue fit for a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City, IA: census context and bilingual headings, plus ingredient accuracy and how descriptions sit with prices
top_problem: This reads as a generic American craft bar with Spanish section labels, not a Mexican cantina. Only 1 of 4 cocktails uses agave (Margarita). There is no mezcal, no Mexican lager (the draft beers are Czech Pilsner, Dry-Hopped IPA and Amber Lager), no Paloma or Ranch Water, and no sin alcohol section. The bilingual heads carry the whole identity, and one of them is filler ('BRANDY · BRANDY'). On top of that, the display italic's swash 'l' makes 'Cócteles' and 'Destilados' read as 'Cócteſes' and 'Destiſados' to a Spanish reader. Every printed fact traces to a row (gateway log_id 260: all 14 approved phg.menu_items for project ddc4bb5b; Junmai Ginjo is status=retired and correctly left off). Glass and garnish match phg.recipe_versions: Margarita Lime wheel/Rocks, Manhattan Cocktail cherry/Coupe, Brown Butter Old Fashioned Orange peel/Rocks, House Daiquiri Lime coin/Coupe. Prices match 14/14 and the tagline '& COCKTAIL BAR · IOWA CITY, IOWA' states no item fact, so both gates pass. Two things hold the score down. First, the beer and wine descriptions are the draft's placeholder taxonomy ('dry red wine' for Malbec, 'dry white wine' for Pinot Grigio). Several also repeat the item name ('hop-forward IPA' under Dry-Hopped IPA, 'toasty amber lager' under Amber Lager, 'dry sparkling cider' under Dry Cider, 'dry sparkling rosé' under Brut Rosé). Second, pricing sits at the top of the market for the area: cocktails are $14-16 while census ZCTA 52240 shows median household income $52,960, median age 28.6 and 29.9% aged 21-34. 52245 and 52246 run $78,020 and $62,521, with 39.1% and 33.1% of households over $100k. Hispanic/Latino share is 11% in 52240 and 5.4-8.3% elsewhere, so the Spanish needs to be exact and idiomatic, not decorative.
fixes: Venue-fit note to Rob and the Coordinator (item lists are not ours to change): a Mexican cantina needs at least one mezcal, a Mexican-style lager on draft, a second agave cocktail and a Sin Alcohol section. These are expected categories and their absence caps criterion 13 in the low 60s whatever the typography does.

Replace the draft's taxonomy beer and wine lines with sourced guest language once Rob fills style, ABV and region. Until then, drop any description that only restates the name (Dry-Hopped IPA 'hop-forward IPA', Amber Lager 'toasty amber lager', Dry Cider 'dry sparkling cider', Brut Rosé 'dry sparkling rosé'), because a name-echo scores lower than no description at all (criterion 12).

Designer: swap the italic cut on the Spanish H2 words so 'l' does not render as a long-s swash ('Cócteles', 'Destilados' currently read 'Cócteſes', 'Destiſados'). Rename the redundant 'BRANDY · BRANDY' sub-head, for example to 'COÑAC · COGNAC', which matches the only item, Cognac VSOP.

Designer: in beer and wine the price hangs off the end of the description, so it lands at a different x on every row (7 / 8 / 7 / 8 in beer; 12 / 11 / 13 in wine). Anchor prices to one column or to the name, as the cocktails do, so price-to-name association is consistent across sections (criterion 14).

Fix the Brown Butter Old Fashioned ingredient line: 'aromatic bitters' is orphaned on its own line with no leading separator. Either tighten the measure so the three ingredients sit on one line or break before 'house demerara syrup'. Also align ingredient capitalisation with the source rows (phg.recipe_versions f06abb74, 9fb77eaa, 7095fd3d, 14d45e57 print Title Case, e.g. 'Tequila Blanco'), or record the lowercase style as a house rule so criterion 11 spelling checks pass cleanly.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together in preview-letter.png (price-to-name tie, description measure and breaks, pour labels), plus ingredient accuracy and venue fit. Verified through the gateway, log_id 264: phg.menu_items for project ddc4bb5b joined to phg.recipe_versions on current_recipe_version_id. All 14 prices match menu_price. Junmai Ginjo is status='retired' (price 12), so leaving it off is correct. Garnish and glass match recipe_versions: Margarita 'Lime wheel'/'Rocks', Manhattan 'Cocktail cherry'/'Coupe', Brown Butter Old Fashioned 'Orange peel'/'Rocks', House Daiquiri 'Lime coin'/'Coupe'. The ingredient lines trace to doc.json components (for example Daiquiri 'Demerara Syrup', role 'House prep', note 'House 1:1 demerara syrup'). The Margarita sensory line traces to its menu_description 'Bright and citrus-forward.'
top_problem: Prices follow two different rules in one menu. Cocktails and spirits put the price 1 em after the name (x 122-157 mm). Beer, cider and wine put it 1 em after a descriptor on the 382 pt tab (x 160.5-171.6 mm). In the Draft block alone, 7 / 8 / 7 sit at three x positions: price right edges 167.1, 170.5 and 173.1 mm, per layout.json. The price reads as the tail of 'crisp pale lager', not of 'Czech Pilsner'. Each price is still on its own row, so the gate passes, but there is no stable price position anywhere. Other problems: Brut Rosé's 13 prints with no glass/bottle label under 'Espumosos · Sparkling', a sub-head that, unlike 'Por copa', says nothing about the pour. The draft does not know the pour and flags it (price_label_unknown), but on paper the price is unlabelled. The Brown Butter Old Fashioned ingredient line breaks after 'house demerara syrup' and leaves 'aromatic bitters' as a widow with no leading separator, so it reads as a second list. Descriptions: 'hop-forward IPA', 'toasty amber lager', 'dry sparkling cider', 'dry sparkling rosé', 'dry red wine' and 'dry white wine' mostly repeat the item name or its class (menu_description rows 'Hop-forward draft IPA.', 'Toasty amber lager.', 'Dry red wine.'). That is taxonomy wording, not guest language. Voice is mixed: the italic 'Bright, citrus-forward' is capitalised and every other line is all lower case. Venue fit: this is a Mexican restaurant, but only 1 of 4 cocktails and 2 of 14 items are agave. The only beer styles are Czech, IPA and amber, and nothing is Mexican. Spanish headers use English title case ('Cerveza y Sidra', 'De Barril', 'Por Copa' should be 'Cerveza y sidra', 'De barril', 'Por copa'), and 'Brandy · Brandy' is a redundant bilingual pair. It reads as a generic American bar with Spanish labels. Criterion 11 is capped only by the known gap: spirits print no age, pour or brand, and beer and wine print no ABV, region or producer. Nothing is invented.
fixes: Give prices one rule on every row: either the name, then the price, then the descriptor for beer, cider and wine, or a fixed price tab (for example 470 pt) shared by all one-row items, so 7 / 8 / 7 / 8 and 12 / 11 / 13 share one right edge and bind to the name.

Stop the Brown Butter Old Fashioned ingredient line from widowing: break it as 'brown butter-washed bourbon · house demerara syrup ·' / 'aromatic bitters', keeping the separator at the end of the line, or rebalance the break so no single item sits alone on a line.
Hold the Brut Rosé price under a pour label ('copa' or 'botella') once Rob answers price_label_unknown, and until then add it to the proposal's needs_input list as a print blocker, not a footnote.

Replace name-repeating descriptors with guest language drawn only from the draft rows (for example keep 'crisp' / 'toasty' / 'hop-forward' but drop the repeated class noun, so 'crisp, pale' rather than 'crisp pale lager'), and capitalise every description line the same way (all sentence case or all lower case).

Use Spanish sentence case in headings ('Cerveza y sidra', 'De barril', 'Por copa', 'Destilados de agave'), drop the 'Brandy · Brandy' doubling (for example 'Brandy · Cognac & Brandy'), and in a note to Rob and the Coordinator flag that the item list is short on agave and Mexican beer for a Mexican restaurant.

lens: How descriptions and prices sit together on the phone preview (preview-phone.png, 1170x6624)
top_problem: On the phone, the beer, cider and wine rows put the price after the descriptor instead of after the name ('Czech Pilsner   crisp pale lager 7'). The cocktails use the opposite pairing, so the menu has two price grammars. Because descriptor lengths vary, the prices also land at ragged x positions (7 / 8 / 7 / 8 / 12 / 11 / 13 drift about 140 px across 7 rows). The descriptors are also near-restatements of the item names ('toasty amber lager' under Amber Lager, 'dry sparkling rosé' under Brut Rosé, 'dry red wine' under Malbec). The result is a Mexican cantina whose drinks list reads like a generic tavern's. All facts are sourced (gateway log_id 265: phg.menu_items project ddc4bb5b; recipe_versions garnish/glassware Margarita 'Lime wheel'/'Rocks', Manhattan 'Cocktail cherry'/'Coupe', Brown Butter Old Fashioned 'Orange peel'/'Rocks', House Daiquiri 'Lime coin'/'Coupe'; beer/wine descs match menu_description 70657e1e, 90b0a7e3, 8fb136cd, 65c39a14, f6f9d57e, 5ba7511f, 32a35bd3; Junmai Ginjo 57617f46 status='retired', so omitting it is correct).
problems: Criterion 14: beer/cider/wine price follows the descriptor at a ragged x (the tab stop fixes the descriptor start, not the price), while cocktail prices follow the name. That is two price-to-name relationships in one menu, and the price reads as belonging to the descriptor.

Criterion 14: draft beers print no pour label and wines print no pour size, and the phone has only the H3 'BY THE GLASS' to tell a guest what $12 buys (missing per doc meta, but no visible flag on the menu).

Criterion 12: 'Amber Lager / toasty amber lager', 'Brut Rosé / dry sparkling rosé', 'Dry Cider / dry sparkling cider' and 'Dry-Hopped IPA / hop-forward IPA' mostly repeat the name. 'dry red wine' and 'dry white wine' are category taxonomy, not guest language.

Criterion 12: only Margarita carries a sensory line, so it is the one italic line on the page and reads as an accident. Its wording 'Bright, citrus-forward' also paraphrases the source 'Bright and citrus-forward.' (menu_items 14555870) instead of quoting it.

Criterion 13: 'BRANDY · BRANDY' is a redundant bilingual pair. 'Destilados' H2 over 'DESTILADOS DE AGAVE' repeats the word. The cantina has no Mexican beer, no mezcal and no non-alcoholic section, so the guest-expected categories for a Mexican restaurant in Iowa City are absent (item list is the venue's, but the menu reads as a generic bar).

Criterion 11: 'house demerara syrup' on the Old Fashioned traces to component role 'House prep / sweetener' (rv 7095fd3d); its menu_description says only 'demerara'. Acceptable but thin. The brown-butter dairy allergen is still unconfirmed (doc meta missing).
fixes: (Designer) Put the price 1 em after the name on beer, cider and wine rows too (descriptor on the tab stop after it), or right-align those prices on one column with a dotted leader, so every price has one relationship to its name.

(Designer) Add pour labels to the draft and wine rows (for example '16 oz', '6 oz glass') as soon as Rob supplies pour size. Until then, flag them in the proposal and do not leave the $ figures unqualified.

Replace name-repeating beer/wine descriptors with sourced sensory language once Rob fills style/region/ABV (for example grape and region for Malbec). Until then, drop descriptors that only restate the name rather than print filler.

Quote the Margarita sensory line exactly from menu_items 14555870 ('Bright and citrus-forward.'), or ask Rob for sensory lines on the other three cocktails so the italic tier reads as a system rather than a one-off.
Rename the 'BRANDY · BRANDY' H3 (for example 'COÑAC · COGNAC' to match the only item) and drop 'Destilados de' from the agave H3 so the Spanish reads natural, not doubled.
